partially_covered.missing: Organization attributes remain limited to address and global location number. No modeling of tax ID, legal form, contact details, or additional identifiers. Coverage unchanged.

Mandatory identifier is modeled, but no explicit enumeration of all D96A-required fields or cardinality constraints. Logical consistency constraints (e.g., sum of line item prices = invoice total) still not formalized in OWL. No SHACL or advanced GCAs.

cq_coverage.details: Coverage is unchanged from previous iteration. The ontology answers nearly all CQs, but lacks full organization attribute modeling and explicit file validity constraints.

strengths: Rich class hierarchy reflecting EDIFACT structure
Good use of equivalence axioms for pivot classes
Functional properties and disjointness are well specified
weaknesses: No general class axioms (GCAs) for advanced validation
Organization attributes are still minimal; key fields (tax ID, legal form, etc.) missing
No modeling of line item taxes or multiple tax rates/types

likely_oops_pitfalls: P4 (Missing domain/range only if extended, currently all defined)
P7 (Inverse properties are generally present, but could be missed if extended)

Introduce general class axioms (GCAs) for validation (medium)

improvement_tracking.notes: No substantive changes from previous iteration. None of the high or medium priority suggestions were implemented. Ontology remains robust for basic EDIFACT invoice modeling, but lacks the depth required for full CQ and constraint coverage.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Expand Organization class to include tax ID, legal form, contact information, and other relevant attributes to fully answer CQ5.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Richer queries about organizations, improved CQ coverage.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Enumerate all mandatory D96A identifiers as explicit properties and add cardinality and logical consistency constraints (e.g., required fields, sum validation) to address CQ13.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Better file format validation and semantic interoperability.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Introduce general class axioms (GCAs) for constraints such as line item price summation and mandatory segment presence.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Enables advanced reasoning and supports SHACL integration.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Model taxes at the line item level and support for multiple tax rates/types for EN 16931-1 compliance.

summary: The ontology remains well-structured and reasoner-friendly, with robust coverage for basic EDIFACT invoice modeling. However, none of the key improvement suggestions from the previous review were implemented, leaving gaps in organization attribute modeling and file validity constraints. Quality and coverage scores are unchanged, and further refinement is needed to reach full CQ and regulatory compliance.
